facts.text: Mount Nittany first appeared on William Scull’s 1770 colonial Pennsylvania map, marking the ridge that would later define Centre County.
The name 'Mount Nittany' derives from an Algonquian word meaning 'single mountain,' reflecting its solitary peak.
In 1907, Penn State student Joe Mason invented the Nittany Lion mascot after a Princeton visit, proclaiming it would defeat the Bengal tiger.
After a mascot‑making company closed in 1990, Elisabeth DeAngelo‑Tucker and her husband John took over production of the Nittany Lion costume.
Mount Nittany is Centre County’s most famous geographical feature, celebrated in local folklore, cultural history, and scenic tours.
Nancy Barrett became the first and only woman to try out for the Nittany Lion mascot in 1996, performing a traditional one‑arm push‑up routine.
